stem: A sensor mounted directly in a dehumidifier discharge reads much drier than sensors in the crop canopy. What is the best interpretation?
choices: The discharge sensor may represent an equipment microclimate rather than the crop environment
The crop is definitely too dry everywhere
The canopy sensors must all be wrong
Dehumidifier discharge should always be the control reference
rationale: Sensor placement affects what condition is measured. Equipment exhaust can create a local microclimate that is not representative of the canopy.
